evidence.excerpt: We should internally store a newtype of encoded strings, or store decoded strings and encode them on the fly.
evidence.interpretation: Review accepts two representations with explicit encoding state, rather than unmarked encoded Strings. The final patch chooses Segment with distinct encoded and encoding constructors.

evidence.excerpt: What in the model depends on this?  `//` is not semantically equivalent to `/` in a Uri, even if they're often the same.
evidence.interpretation: Review challenges implicit normalization. Author subsequently proposes explicit normalize and acknowledges the fix; this is not evidence of complete losslessness for every trailing-slash edge in the historical implementation.
evidence.author: rossabaker

evidence.excerpt: I think an asymmetric equals, which violates both the laws of Scala and Java, would be more problematic in the long run.
evidence.interpretation: Review rejects preserving String-alias behavior via asymmetric equals and suggests a Scalafix lint/fix instead; migration ergonomics do not justify violating equality symmetry.

lazy val tests = libraryProject("tests")
  .enablePlugins(NoPublishPlugin)
  .settings(
    description := "Tests for core project",
    startYear := Some(2013),
  )
  .dependsOn(core, testing % "test->test")
evidence.interpretation: Source observation: core contract tests live in a separate tests project so they can depend on published testing helpers. Test discovery must follow module ownership, not assume core/test contains the regression suite.
Source observation: Segment.apply encodes a raw value; Segment.encoded preserves an already encoded value. Confusing these constructors double-encodes percent sequences or loses segment boundaries.
Source observation: Path equality only accepts another Path and compares segments and both flags. The obsolete String-alias equality is not emulated.
Source observation: this historical suite registers Order and Semigroup law checks, not a Monoid. Presence of a suite is not evidence that this run executed it.
Source observation: regression examples distinguish parsing already encoded URI segments from appending decoded segment text containing a slash.

claims.rule: When changing URI path representation, distinguish encoded segments from decoded inputs, test delimiters and empty segments, preserve equality symmetry, and use explicit migration support rather than String-compatible asymmetric equals.
claims.applicability: Applies to path construction/parsing, routing refactors and alias-to-wrapper migration. The 2020 evidence establishes review intent and selected regressions, not complete correctness of that historical Path implementation.
claims.counterexample: An application may deliberately normalize repeated slashes at an explicit routing boundary. Do not prohibit such policy or demand a Monoid merely because concatenation has a Semigroup.
